subject.title: [Bug/Docs]: local+hybrid memory_search quality can appear unstable due to extraPaths path drift + benchmark-file contamination

question: Should OpenClaw add a public `memorySearch` exclusion/path-hygiene contract now, and should it be builtin-only first or cover QMD, status diagnostics, and docs in one decision?
rationale: This cannot be resolved as a narrow bug fix because it adds public config and changes which files enter durable recall, while repository policy treats config/default and memory/session-state surfaces as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Repair narrow builtin exclusion first
options.body: Repair and land the open `excludePaths` PR with merged config semantics, index-identity coverage, and explicit builtin-only docs while tracking QMD and diagnostic parity separately.

options.title: Require cross-backend contract
options.body: Pause the open PR until builtin indexing, QMD collections, watcher behavior, docs, and status diagnostics share one exclusion/path-hygiene model.

options.title: Docs and diagnostics only
options.body: Defer public exclusion config and improve `memory status` plus docs guidance around path drift, broad `extraPaths`, and benchmark contamination.

recommendation.title: Repair narrow builtin exclusion first
recommendation.body: Repair and land the open `excludePaths` PR with merged config semantics, index-identity coverage, and explicit builtin-only docs while tracking QMD and diagnostic parity separately.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest available owner for the memory host SDK and manager-state boundary where config, indexing, and reindex semantics meet.
